exposure: Delivery method (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Brain white matter microstructural integrity (fractional anisotropy and diffusivity values)
cohort: The study included 68 preterm infants (23 vaginally delivered, 45 C-section) without neuroimaging abnormality on pre-discharge term-equivalent MRI.
finding: Preterm infants delivered via C-section showed significantly lower fractional anisotropy and higher diffusivity values across major white matter tracts compared to those delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Preterm infants delivered by C-section exhibited poorer brain white matter microstructural integrity compared to those delivered vaginally.
followup_time: Around term-equivalent age (at pre-discharge term-equivalent MRI)
birth_weight: Measured and considered as a covariate; lower birth weight among C-section infants was a partial mediator.
gest_age: Preterm infants, specific range not provided.
